column1: # planning/fidelity/servers.pairing.tsv — which build node answers which mock affordance.
# Four tab-separated columns:  state <TAB> affordance <TAB> node <TAB> citation
# This file declares ONLY the pairing. It never declares a status: present, divergent, absent and
# unclassified are computed by scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py from the two artifacts on every
# run, which is what makes `present` earned by measuring rather than asserted. Deleting a line here
# does not delete a row from the ledger — the mock side of the inventory is derived from the mock
# on every run, so an affordance with no line becomes `absent`, which is a finding.
#   node = -            the affordance has no counterpart in the build
#   affordance = +path  a build node with no counterpart in the mock, cited
# A citation is external and pre-existing: a file and the claim it already makes. A justification
# composed while filling this in is motivated classification wearing a citation's clothes, and the
# row is a defect either way — a citation records WHO OWNS the difference, and never suppresses it.
# What this file is not: a conversion. The Servers board in the build was written against DESIGN.md
# (Instrument Panel, breaker column) and the mock draws Patchbay (signal path, jack lane, inspector).
# M16 owns that supersession and M17 owns the four states' copy. This ledger is the measurement that
# says how far apart they are today, filled before either of those items starts.
